chunks.title: Landmark Precedents in Indian Family & Matrimonial Jurisprudence
chunks.content: # Landmark Precedents in Indian Family & Matrimonial Jurisprudence

chunks.title: Rajnesh v. Neha, (2021) 2 SCC 324
chunks.content:
### Rajnesh v. Neha, (2021) 2 SCC 324
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (Indu Malhotra, J.)
**Core Holding:** Established nationwide uniform guidelines for determining maintenance in matrimonial proceedings. Mandated that both parties must file comprehensive Affidavits of Assets and Liabilities covering income, properties, debts, standard of living, and expenses. Overlapping maintenance claims across HMA, DV Act, and CrPC §125 must be adjusted and set off.

chunks.title: Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli, (2006) 4 SCC 558
chunks.content:
### Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli, (2006) 4 SCC 558
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** Held that sustained course of abusive conduct, false criminal complaints, and public humiliation constitute mental cruelty of such gravity that human endurance cannot reasonably be expected to tolerate it. While irretrievable breakdown is not an express statutory ground under HMA §13, prolonged severe acrimony amounts to mental cruelty.

chunks.title: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511
chunks.content:
### Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** Formulated illustrative principles on mental cruelty: mere trivial irritations and normal wear and tear of marriage are not cruelty, but sustained coldness, willful denial of marital relations without valid medical justification, and prolonged separation coupled with hostility establish legal cruelty.

chunks.title: Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja, (2020) 10 SCC 788
chunks.content:
### Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja, (2020) 10 SCC 788
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (Ashok Bhushan, J.)
**Core Holding:** Overruled earlier narrow interpretations of "shared household" under the DV Act. Held that an aggrieved daughter-in-law has a statutory right of residence in a household where she lived in a domestic relationship, even if the property belongs exclusively to the father-in-law or mother-in-law.

chunks.title: Gaurav Nagpal v. Sumedha Nagpal, (2009) 1 SCC 42
chunks.content:
### Gaurav Nagpal v. Sumedha Nagpal, (2009) 1 SCC 42
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** Reaffirmed that the paramount consideration in child custody disputes is the "welfare of the child" — encompassing moral, physical, emotional, and educational well-being — which supersedes pure proprietary claims or financial superiority of either parent.

chunks.title: Procedural Practice Notes — Family Law & Domestic Adjudication
chunks.content: # Procedural Practice Notes — Family Law & Domestic Adjudication

chunks.title: Standard of Proof & Evidentiary Thresholds
chunks.content:
### Standard of Proof & Evidentiary Thresholds
1. **Preponderance of Probabilities:** Unlike criminal trials, matrimonial disputes under the Hindu Marriage Act and Special Marriage Act are governed by the civil standard of preponderance of probabilities.
2. **Standard on Cruelty & Desertion:** Requires cogent circumstantial or documentary corroboration (medical records, correspondence, proof of independent residence, police complaints) demonstrating an intolerable matrimonial atmosphere.

chunks.title: Mandatory Pre-Trial Mediation & Reconciliation
chunks.content:
### Mandatory Pre-Trial Mediation & Reconciliation
1. Under Section 9 of the Family Courts Act 1984 and HMA Section 23(2), the Family Court is statutorily obligated to endeavor to bring about reconciliation between the spouses before proceeding to contentious trial.
2. If mediation fails, the court frames specific legal issues regarding cruelty, desertion, quantum of maintenance, and child custody.

chunks.title: Interim Protections & Affidavits of Disclosure
chunks.content:
### Interim Protections & Affidavits of Disclosure
1. Applications under Section 24 HMA or Section 12 DV Act require filing of Rajnesh v. Neha asset disclosure affidavits within 4 weeks.
2. Ex-parte interim protection orders under Section 23 DV Act may be granted upon prima facie showing of imminent domestic violence or economic dispossession.

chunks.title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (HMA) Section 13 — Divorce Grounds
Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 13B — Divorce by Mutual Consent
chunks.content:
### Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 13B — Divorce by Mutual Consent
(1) A petition for dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce may be presented to the district court by both the parties to a marriage together, on the ground that they have been living separately for a period of one year or more, that they have not been able to live together and that they have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved.

chunks.title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 24 & 25 — Maintenance Pendente Lite and Permanent Alimony
chunks.content:
### Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 24 & 25 — Maintenance Pendente Lite and Permanent Alimony
- Section 24 provides interim maintenance and expenses of proceedings where either spouse has no independent income sufficient for their support.
- Section 25 empowers the court to award gross sum or monthly maintenance having regard to the respondent's income, property, and conduct of the parties.

chunks.title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (PWDVA)
chunks.content:
### Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (PWDVA)
- **Section 3:** Definition of domestic violence including physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, and economic abuse.
- **Section 12:** Application to Magistrate for protection orders, residence orders, and monetary relief.
- **Section 19:** Residence orders protecting the aggrieved woman's right to reside in the shared household regardless of legal title.
- **Section 20:** Monetary reliefs including medical expenses, loss of earnings, and maintenance for the aggrieved woman and her children.

chunks.title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 (SMA) Section 27 — Divorce
chunks.content:
### Special Marriage Act, 1954 (SMA) Section 27 — Divorce
Provides secular grounds for divorce including adultery, desertion for two years, imprisonment for seven years, and cruelty for marriages registered under the Special Marriage Act.

chunks.title: Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 Section 7 & 17 — Minor's Custody
chunks.content:
### Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 Section 7 & 17 — Minor's Custody
Section 17 mandates that in appointing or declaring the guardian of a minor, the Court shall be guided by what appears to be for the welfare of the minor, considering age, sex, religion, and the wishes of a capable minor.
